comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== BLOCKING DISCOVERY BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION: THIS TICKET'S CENTRAL PREMISE NO LONGER HOLDS. ===
Claimed and investigated; NOT implemented, because implementing the plan as written would ship
~20 annotations that enforce NOTHING. Recording the measurement rather than proceeding.

THE TICKET'S PROOF DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Its three-way probe asserts that
`def f(client: TicketTransport)` calling an undeclared member yields
`error: "TicketTransport" has no attribute ...  [attr-defined]`. Run today under the repo's own
settings (`mypy src/rebar`, i.e. exactly what `make typecheck` runs — every file NAMED on the
command line, which matters because `follow_imports = "silent"` reports only on named files), it
produces **NO ERROR AT ALL**. Not for a real member, and not for `definitely_not_a_member`.

THE CAUSE, ISOLATED WITH A CONTROLLED PROBE. Two functions in one file, one parameter each:

    class PlainPort(Protocol):
        def get_issue(self, remote_id: str) -> dict: ...

    def via_metaclass_protocol(client: TicketTransport) -> None:
        client.definitely_not_a_member("x")      # -> NO ERROR
    def via_plain_protocol(client: PlainPort) -> None:
        client.definitely_not_a_member("x")      # -> error: "PlainPort" has no attribute ...

Only the plain Protocol errors. The difference is
`class TicketTransport(Protocol, metaclass=_TransportPortMeta)` (`_backend.py:184`, with
`# type: ignore[misc]` on the metaclass at `:127`) — **the custom metaclass makes mypy stop
attribute-checking the annotated type.** The `type: ignore[misc]` is the visible symptom: mypy
does not model this construct, and silently degrades the annotated parameter rather than
complaining at the use site.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THE TICKET. The plan's whole thesis is "annotate as the
PORT, not as `Any`, because `Any` satisfies the ratchet while staying blind". Against the current
`TicketTransport`, **annotating as the port is ALSO blind** — it just looks rigorous. That is the
same failure the ticket was written to prevent, arriving by a route the ticket did not anticipate,
and it would be invisible in review: the diff would show twenty correct-looking annotations and
`make typecheck` would stay green because it was never going to say anything.

WHERE THE METACLASS CAME FROM, so it is not removed casually. `_TransportPortMeta` is J9's
([rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]) and its docstring gives the reason: `typing`'s own `isinstance`
against a runtime-checkable Protocol goes through `ABCMeta`'s subclass CACHE, which memoises the
first positive answer, so a class that conformed once keeps reporting `True` after a member is
removed — fatal for a guard whose job is detecting a missing member. The metaclass makes the
RUNTIME check uncached and therefore honest. It is load-bearing for `assert_transport_conforms`.

SO THE REAL DECISION THIS TICKET MUST MAKE — and it is a design fork, not an implementation
detail:
  (a) give mypy a checkable view while keeping the runtime guard — e.g. declare the Protocol
      PLAINLY and attach the uncached-`isinstance` behaviour to a separate runtime subclass or a
      standalone conformance function, so static and runtime checking do not compete for the same
      class object; or
  (b) accept STATIC blindness and rely on J9's runtime `assert_transport_conforms()` alone, in
      which case this ticket's premise is retired and it closes as not-a-bug with the finding
      recorded — the annotations would still be worth doing for readability and for Serena/Pyright
      navigation (bug dbf9), but NOT as an enforcement mechanism, and the plan must stop claiming
      they are.
Either way the plan needs rewriting before code is written; (a) is the substantive option and
needs its own verification that the split does not weaken the runtime guard bda8 added.

STATUS: claimed, plan certified, NOT implemented. Nothing pushed. The working tree is clean — the
probe file was removed after each measurement (`git status --porcelain` empty, verified).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== RESOLUTION OF THE BLOCKING DISCOVERY: the premise HOLDS. The metaclass was not the cause. ===
The previous comment's measurement was CONFOUNDED BY THE IMPORT PATH, not caused by
`_TransportPortMeta`. Neither fork (a) nor (b) is needed: the plan stands, with one added
requirement. Description rewritten accordingly. No production code written; worktree clean.

THE COUNTER-EXPERIMENT. The prior probe compared `TicketTransport` (reached via
`from rebar_reconciler._backend import ...`) against a Protocol declared LOCALLY in the same probe
file, and attributed the difference to the metaclass. Two variables moved. Holding the import path
constant instead, in ONE file under `mypy src/rebar` (mypy 2.3.0, repo settings):

    from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_shim
    from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_real
    def f(a: TT_shim, b: TT_real) -> None:
        reveal_type(a)   # -> Revealed type is "Any"
        reveal_type(b)   # -> "rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend.TicketTransport"
        a.definitely_not_a_member("x")   # -> NO ERROR
        b.definitely_not_a_member("x")   # -> error: "TicketTransport" has no attribute ... [attr-defined]

SAME CLASS, SAME METACLASS, OPPOSITE OUTCOMES. The cause is that `rebar_reconciler` is not an
importable package -- it is a top-level name created at runtime by injecting `src/rebar/_engine`
on `sys.path` -- so with `ignore_missing_imports = true` mypy widens everything imported through it
to `Any`. Confirmed: `python -c "import rebar_reconciler"` -> ModuleNotFoundError.

THE FIX IS THE IMPORT FORM, NOT A CLASS SPLIT. Inside a reconciler module, a relative import
restores the check against today's unmodified `TicketTransport`:

    # src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_probe.py
    from ._backend import TicketTransport
    def f(a: TicketTransport) -> None:
        a.definitely_not_a_member("x")        # -> [attr-defined]   (enforcement works)
        a.set_entity_property("K-1","p",1)    # -> no error         (no false positives)

Composition survives the metaclass too: `class X(TicketTransport, SupportsComments, Protocol)` is
attribute-checked normally.

WHY (a) IS UNNECESSARY AND (b) WOULD HAVE BEEN A MISTAKE. (a) proposed splitting the Protocol to
stop static and runtime checking competing for one class object -- but they were never competing;
the measurement that suggested they were was confounded. Splitting would have churned a
load-bearing runtime guard for no static gain. (b) would have retired a TRUE premise on a false
measurement and downgraded ~20 annotations to cosmetics.

THE RUNTIME GUARD IS UNTOUCHED, AND ITS RATIONALE INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED:
    plain @runtime_checkable Protocol, conforming     -> isinstance True
    plain ... after delattr of a member               -> isinstance True   <- ABCMeta cache lies
    TicketTransport (metaclass), conforming           -> isinstance True
    TicketTransport after delattr                     -> isinstance False  <- uncached, honest
    assert_transport_conforms(), after delattr        -> raises BackendEnvError
So `_TransportPortMeta` earns its keep for the `isinstance` spelling the held-out tests use, and
`assert_transport_conforms()` is `hasattr`-based and cache-immune by construction. This story
changes NEITHER.

SIZING PROBE (run, then reverted). Annotating `client` on `dispatch_one.create_one` and
`update_one` with a relatively-imported `TicketTransport` yielded exactly ONE new error:
`"TicketTransport" has no attribute "add_comment"` at dispatch_one.py:461. That is a REAL finding
of the a357 class that the existing AST audit structurally CANNOT report, because `add_comment` is
one of the four capability members the metaclass carries as a metaclass attribute, so
`hasattr(TicketTransport, "add_comment")` is True while mypy (which does not consult metaclass
attributes for a Protocol-typed value) correctly does not. mypy is strictly stronger than the audit
here. Resolution at such sites is a composed view -- verified to type-check:
`class _CommentingTransport(TicketTransport, SupportsComments, Protocol): ...` -- NOT adding the
member to the port body (which would oblige every future transport to provide it).

WHAT THE PLAN GAINED. The requirement is now "annotate as the port AND import the port by a path
mypy resolves". The shim-import route is a SECOND way this change can self-neutralise while looking
correct in review, so the blindness guard test and the ACs now pin both routes, and an AC requires
`reveal_type` evidence that each touched module's annotation is not silently `Any`.

STATUS: claimed, description rewritten, NOT implemented, nothing pushed, `git status --porcelain`
empty (every probe file removed and dispatch_one.py restored from backup, verified).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== CORRECTION, FROM THE AUTHOR OF THE "BLOCKING DISCOVERY" COMMENT ABOVE: IT IS WRONG. ===
That comment says this ticket's premise is false and instructs the reader NOT to implement the
plan. Disregard it. The premise is TRUE. I have re-verified the refutation myself rather than
taking it on trust, and the corrected analysis is in the counter-experiment comment.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, AND WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING. My probe moved TWO variables at once. It reached
`TicketTransport` through `from rebar_reconciler._backend import ...` while comparing it against a
`PlainPort` I declared LOCALLY in the same probe file. I then attributed the difference to the one
I was looking for — the `_TransportPortMeta` metaclass — when the actual cause was the IMPORT PATH.
That is an uncontrolled experiment, and it produced a confident, specific, wrong conclusion that I
recorded as established and used to halt the ticket. It is exactly the failure this epic's own
standing rule warns about ("verify mechanisms, not plausibility"), committed while I was applying
that rule elsewhere.

THE CONTROLLED VERSION, run in ONE file so only the import path varies (`mypy src/rebar`, the same
command `make typecheck` runs):

    from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_real
    from rebar_reconciler._backend        import TicketTransport as TT_shim

    def via_shim(a: TT_shim): reveal_type(a)   # -> "Any"                     ; bogus call: NO ERROR
    def via_real(b: TT_real): reveal_type(b)   # -> "...TicketTransport"      ; bogus call: [attr-defined]

Same class. Same metaclass. Opposite outcomes. **The metaclass is exonerated.**

THE REAL MECHANISM: `rebar_reconciler` is not an importable package — it is a top-level name
created at RUNTIME by injecting `src/rebar/_engine` onto `sys.path`. Confirmed directly:
`python -c "import rebar_reconciler"` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. With
`ignore_missing_imports = true` (set globally in `pyproject.toml`), mypy widens everything imported
through that name to `Any`. Every intra-package import in the reconciler uses that form, so the
blindness is repo-wide and has nothing to do with any Protocol's definition.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE TICKET: the requirement is not "annotate as the port" but **"annotate as
the port AND import the port by a path mypy can resolve"**. Annotating alone would have produced
exactly the silent no-op I wrongly blamed on the metaclass — so the conclusion "do not implement"
was wrong while the instinct behind it (these annotations could easily enforce nothing) was right.
The rewritten plan now requires `reveal_type` evidence that no annotation has silently degraded to
`Any`, which is the assertion that makes the difference observable.

Also worth carrying: sizing showed mypy is strictly STRONGER than the existing AST audit here. With
`client` annotated on `dispatch_one.create_one`/`update_one`, mypy reports
`"TicketTransport" has no attribute "add_comment"` at `dispatch_one.py:461` — a genuine a357-class
finding the audit CANNOT report, because `add_comment` is a metaclass-carried capability member so
`hasattr(TicketTransport, "add_comment")` is True while mypy correctly disagrees.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION OF THE REWRITTEN PLAN'S LINCHPIN. It holds. Run by a different
session than the one that wrote the counter-experiment, deliberately, because this ticket has
already produced one confidently-recorded WRONG conclusion and the whole plan now rests on this one
claim.

Probe placed INSIDE the package (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_cc77_probe.py), so the only
variable between the two functions is the IMPORT PATH — same class, same metaclass, same file, same
command (mypy src/rebar, i.e. what make typecheck runs). Measured at df41edcf25:

    from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_shim   # absolute, via sys.path shim
    from ._backend            import TicketTransport as TT_rel         # relative

    def via_shim(a: TT_shim):
        reveal_type(a)                        -> Revealed type is "Any"
        a.definitely_not_a_member("x")         -> NO ERROR

    def via_relative(b: TT_rel):
        reveal_type(b)                        -> "rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend.TicketTransport"
        b.definitely_not_a_member("x")         -> error: "TicketTransport" has no attribute
                                                 "definitely_not_a_member"  [attr-defined]
        b.set_entity_property("K-1", "p", 1)   -> NO ERROR

THREE THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES, and the third is the one that matters most:
 1. ENFORCEMENT WORKS through a relative import — the bogus member is caught.
 2. NO FALSE POSITIVES — set_entity_property, a genuinely declared member, is accepted. So the
    annotation does not merely make mypy shout at everything; it discriminates.
 3. THE METACLASS IS EXONERATED, confirmed rather than taken on trust. The [attr-defined] error is
    against TODAY'S TicketTransport with _TransportPortMeta still attached. So the earlier
    'BLOCKING DISCOVERY' conclusion — that the class must be split before this story can proceed —
    is refuted by direct measurement, and the plan is right to leave the metaclass alone. Splitting
    a load-bearing runtime guard on the strength of a confounded probe would have been the
    expensive mistake here.

The probe file was removed immediately after measurement; git status is clean. Recording the
measurement rather than the file so the result survives without leaving a stray module in the tree.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== AC3: NEGATIVE mypy PROBE, RUN AND RECORDED. The annotation enforces something. ===
Probe placed INSIDE the package (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_cc77_probe.py) so the ONLY
variable between the two functions is the import path — same class, same metaclass, same file, one
command (mypy src/rebar, i.e. what make typecheck runs). Removed immediately after measurement.

    from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_shim   # sys.path shim
    from ._backend                import TicketTransport as TT_rel     # relative

    def via_shim(a: TT_shim) -> None:
        reveal_type(a)
        a.definitely_not_a_member('x')

    def via_relative(b: TT_rel) -> None:
        reveal_type(b)
        b.definitely_not_a_member('x')
        b.set_entity_property('K-1', 'p', 1)

VERBATIM mypy OUTPUT (ANSI stripped):

    _cc77_probe.py:9:  note: Revealed type is "Any"
    _cc77_probe.py:14: note: Revealed type is "rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend.TicketTransport"
    _cc77_probe.py:15: error: "TicketTransport" has no attribute "definitely_not_a_member"  [attr-defined]

THREE THINGS, and note what is ABSENT:
 1. via_shim line 10 (a.definitely_not_a_member) produced NO OUTPUT AT ALL. Not an error, not a
    note. The shim-imported annotation is silently Any.
 2. via_relative line 15 IS an [attr-defined] error — enforcement works, against TODAY'S
    TicketTransport with _TransportPortMeta still attached. The metaclass is exonerated a third
    time, now by an independent session.
 3. via_relative line 16 (set_entity_property, a genuinely declared member) produced NO error. So
    the annotation DISCRIMINATES; it does not merely make mypy shout at everything. That absence
    is the load-bearing half — an annotation that errors on everything would be useless.

=== AC2: reveal_type EVIDENCE FOR EVERY TOUCHED MODULE. No annotation silently degraded. ===
One port parameter per touched module, probed in a single mypy run, then reverted. 14/14 resolve to
the REAL type; ZERO report Any:

    applier.apply                                  -> ...TicketTransport | None
    apply_inbound._apply_inbound_create            -> ...TicketTransport | None
    apply_inbound_records._inbound_create_writeback_jira -> ...TicketTransport
    apply_outbound._apply_outbound_create          -> ...TicketTransport | None
    batch_dispatch.delete_one                      -> ...TicketTransport
    binding_store._current_key_by_id               -> ...TicketTransport
    binding_walk.compute_binding_walk_mutations    -> ...TicketTransport
    dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter -> ...TicketTransport
    dispatch_one.create_one                        -> ...TicketTransport
    fetcher._iter_pages                            -> ...TicketTransport
    outbound_assignee._bootstrap_account_id_via_user_search -> ...TicketTransport
    outbound_comments._diff_comments               -> ...TicketTransport | None
    outbound_differ._safe_get_issue                -> ...TicketTransport
    typed_dispatch._apply_typed                    -> ...TicketTransport | None

(each '...' is the literal prefix rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend.)

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== AC4: THE COMPLETE [attr-defined] LIST FROM THE ANNOTATION PASS, AND EACH ONE'S RESOLUTION ===
Measured BEFORE resolving anything (plan step 3), by annotating every bare/Any client|transport
param in the core at once and running mypy src/rebar. FOUR [attr-defined] errors, and sixteen
[assignment] errors. That is the whole list; nothing is omitted.

--- CLASS A: 4 x [attr-defined] — ALL FOUR are opt-in capability members ---
  1. dispatch_one.py:465  "TicketTransport" has no attribute "add_comment"       (in create_one)
  2. dispatch_one.py:667  "TicketTransport" has no attribute "add_comment"       (in _update_one_scalar_update)
  3. dispatch_one.py:752  "TicketTransport" has no attribute "set_relationship"  (in _update_one_dispatch_links)
  4. dispatch_apply_phases.py:165 "TicketTransport" has no attribute "add_comment" (in _update_one_dispatch_comments)

RESOLUTION — all four NARROWED to the capability Protocol that declares the member:
  1,2,4 -> cast("SupportsComments", client).add_comment(...)
  3     -> _call_with_retry(cast("SupportsLinks", client).set_relationship, ...)
NONE resolved by widening to Any. NONE by reverting an import to the rebar_reconciler. path. NONE
by adding the member to TicketTransport's body (that would oblige every future transport to provide
an opt-in feature). The narrowed value stays attribute-checked — a typo in the member name is still
an [attr-defined] error — so this is a narrowing, not an escape. The cast target is a STRING forward
reference, so the SupportsComments/SupportsLinks import stays under TYPE_CHECKING and nothing changes
at runtime. The rationale is written once, next to the four members, in _backend.py.

AN INDEPENDENT FINDING, worth carrying: NONE of the four sites has a runtime capability guard. The
core calls add_comment / set_relationship unconditionally, unlike fetcher.py:553/:590 which do gate
get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map behind hasattr. It is safe today only because the differ that
populates the mutation is itself capability-gated upstream — an invariant nothing local asserts.
mypy is the only one of the three checks that can see these sites at all: the AST audit cannot,
because hasattr(TicketTransport, 'add_comment') is True via the metaclass. First concrete
confirmation that mypy is strictly STRONGER than the audit here, as the plan predicted.

--- CLASS B: 16 x [assignment] 'Incompatible default for parameter (default has type None)' ---
applier.py:385; apply_inbound.py:65,133,173,282,309,335,352; apply_outbound.py:91,124,163,183,206;
binding_store.py:557; outbound_comments.py:167; typed_dispatch.py:100.
RESOLUTION: annotated 'TicketTransport | None' — these parameters genuinely default to None and
every one of the bodies already guards 'if client is None'. This produced ZERO follow-on errors,
which is itself the evidence that the Optional is honest rather than papered over: had any body
dereferenced client unconditionally, mypy would have reported it.

AFTER RESOLUTION: mypy src/rebar is clean (413 files). No new type: ignore was added anywhere.

--- SCALE ACTUALLY ANNOTATED ---
38 port parameters across 14 core modules: 29 were BARE, 9 were annotated 'Any'. (The ticket's
15/10 sizing counted a narrower slice.) One deliberate Any REMAINS and is pinned by an assertion:
_backend.assert_transport_conforms(transport: Any) — it is the runtime guard itself, whose job is to
inspect an object that may NOT conform; annotating it as the port would assert the very property it
exists to check.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== AC5: THE BLINDNESS GUARD, MUTATION-VERIFIED. It can actually fail, for the right reason. ===
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_transport_param_typing_cc77.py — an AST check over every core
reconciler module (adapters/ excluded: they IMPLEMENT the port rather than consume it).

A test that has never been seen red is not evidence. Each of the three bad spellings was applied to
a REAL parameter (dispatch_one.create_one's client) and the suite re-run:

  MUTATION 1  client            (bare)            -> 1 failed, 56 passed
  MUTATION 2  client: Any                         -> 1 failed, 56 passed
  MUTATION 3  from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport  (shim path)
                                                  -> 1 failed, 56 passed
  RESTORED                                        -> 57 passed

Every failure is 'AssertionError: port-typing violations:' raised at the test's own assert, in the
parametrised case [dispatch_one.py] — i.e. the check FIRED. Not an AttributeError, not an
ImportError, not a collection error. Mutation 3 matters most: it is the only one where the source
still reads 'client: TicketTransport' and mypy still passes clean, so nothing else in the repo
would have caught it.

The exemption set is a single pinned entry, asserted by a second test so it cannot quietly grow into
an allowlist; that test also re-derives the exempt function from the AST, so a stale exemption fails
rather than silently covering nothing.

=== AC6: NOTHING WAS WEAKENED ===
git diff origin/main..HEAD touches _backend.py only by APPENDING a comment block. _TransportPortMeta,
assert_transport_conforms(), the required-member list, and the AST audit are byte-unchanged (no diff
hunk intersects them). Reconciler unit suite: 1821 passed, 1 xfailed, UNEDITED — no test needed
changing, which is the change's own premise (annotations + import form only, zero behaviour).

=== MODULE SIZES (800 hard cap) — one real constraint hit, and how it was resolved ===
dispatch_one.py sat at 796/800 BEFORE this change, so its six annotations (+7 lines, mostly one
signature ruff must explode past 100 cols) did NOT fit. Resolved by moving the two PURE link-probe
helpers (_index_existing_links / _find_link_id) to dispatch_apply_phases.py — the leaf that already
holds update_one's other extracted phases — and re-importing them, so dispatch_one.<name> attribute
access and bare-name calls resolve unchanged. They depend on nothing in dispatch_one.

  dispatch_one.py           796 -> 759
  dispatch_apply_phases.py  170 -> 226
  _backend.py               599 -> 622
  applier.py                795 -> 800 (at the cap, under it; gate is strictly '>')
  outbound_differ.py        792 -> 799
  all others                well under

A FIRST attempt also moved _call_with_retry into a new leaf. It is NOT behaviour-neutral and was
ABANDONED: 6 tests monkeypatch dispatch_one.time / dispatch_one.RetryExhaustedError, which
_call_with_retry reads as module globals, so relocating it silently changes what those patches
affect. Recording the rejected route so nobody re-attempts it: _call_with_retry stays in dispatch_one.

Also measured and rejected: a RUNTIME relative import ('from ._backend import ...'). It breaks 10
tests with 'attempted relative import with no known parent package' — several test modules load
reconciler modules by file path, with no parent package. The port import must be TYPE_CHECKING-
guarded, and capability narrowing must use a STRING cast target so no runtime import is needed.
Both facts are non-obvious and cost a full suite run each to find.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== AC6 VERIFIED MECHANICALLY, not by eye, and one CI trap worth carrying ===
Extracted the three guard symbols from origin/main and from HEAD by AST span and compared bytes:

    TicketTransport            BYTE-IDENTICAL (5378 bytes)
    _TransportPortMeta         BYTE-IDENTICAL (3150 bytes)
    assert_transport_conforms  BYTE-IDENTICAL (1669 bytes)

_backend.py's ONLY change is an appended comment block. No existing test file is touched — the sole
test diff is the new guard (+190 lines, 0 deletions). Backend contract / capability / neutrality /
port-completeness / DC-port / transport-exception suites: 110 passed.

--- CI TRAP: docs/env-vars.md pins LINE NUMBERS, so a pure annotation change breaks a gate ---
Changes 1222-1225 took Verified-1 on patchset 1. The failing step was the 'Env-var registry drift
gate' on ALL FOUR matrix jobs (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 + macos py3.13) — deterministic, not a flake,
so no 'recheck' would have helped.

docs/env-vars.md is DERIVED by scanning env-var reads under src/rebar and records each read's
file:LINE. Adding import lines to apply_inbound.py, binding_store.py and outbound_differ.py shifted
three recorded lines by 2-3, and the committed registry went stale. Nothing about the change is
env-var related; the coupling is purely positional.

The non-obvious part: Gerrit CI verifies EACH change in a stack independently, so regenerating the
registry once at the tip is NOT enough — the intermediate patchsets stay red. Fixed by regenerating
inside the rebase so every commit carries a consistent registry:

    git rebase origin/main --exec 'python scripts/gen_env_registry.py && \
      { git diff --quiet -- docs/env-vars.md || \
        { git add docs/env-vars.md && git commit --amend --no-edit; }; }'

(--amend --no-edit preserves each Change-Id; verified all four survived.) Then re-ran the gate as an
--exec over the stack and confirmed GATE-OK on all four patchsets before re-pushing.

Any future change that merely ADDS OR REMOVES LINES above an os.environ read in src/rebar will hit
this. Worth knowing before spending a CI round-trip on it.

compiled_state.description:
## Claim

The core reconciler passes its transport around as an UNANNOTATED parameter. That is why the Backend
port can silently under-declare what the core requires — the defect class behind
[rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5], where a DC writing reconcile pass crashed on a method
(`set_entity_property`) that the core calls from three sites and `TicketTransport` never declared.

This is not an adjacent tidiness issue. It is the ENABLING CONDITION.

## Proof — three-way mypy probe (RE-VERIFIED, and the enabling detail it omitted)

    def current_shape(client, ...):                     # today's core
        client.set_entity_property(...)                 # -> NO ERROR

    def annotated_any(client: Any, ...):                # what the ratchet alone accepts
        client.set_entity_property(...)                 # -> NO ERROR

    def annotated_port(client: TicketTransport, ...):   # typed as the PORT
        client.definitely_not_a_member(...)
        # -> error: "TicketTransport" has no attribute "definitely_not_a_member"  [attr-defined]

Run with the repo's own settings — `mypy src/rebar`, i.e. exactly what `make typecheck` runs.

**The third row only holds when mypy can RESOLVE the annotation, and inside this package that is
not automatic.** Every core reconciler module imports its siblings absolutely as
`from rebar_reconciler.X import …` (87 such imports), because the package is executed as the
top-level name `rebar_reconciler` with `src/rebar/_engine` injected on `sys.path`. mypy is never
told about that injection, `rebar_reconciler` is not an importable distribution, and
`ignore_missing_imports = true` is set — so **`from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport`
resolves to `Any`**, and a parameter annotated with it is exactly as blind as `client: Any`.
Measured with `reveal_type`, both forms in one file:

    from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_shim
    from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_real
    def f(a: TT_shim, b: TT_real) -> None:
        reveal_type(a)   # -> "Any"                    <- silently unchecked
        reveal_type(b)   # -> "rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend.TicketTransport"

A **relative** import inside a reconciler module resolves correctly and restores the check:

    # src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/<any module>.py
    from ._backend import TicketTransport
    def f(a: TicketTransport) -> None:
        a.definitely_not_a_member("x")       # -> error: ... has no attribute ...  [attr-defined]
        a.set_entity_property("K-1", "p", 1) # -> no error

So the requirement is sharper than the original plan stated: **annotate as the port AND import the
port by a path mypy resolves.** Getting only the first half ships annotations that look rigorous and
enforce nothing — the exact failure this ticket exists to prevent, arriving by a different route.

## The metaclass is NOT the obstacle (a prior blocking finding on this ticket, now refuted)

An earlier investigation recorded that
`class TicketTransport(Protocol, metaclass=_TransportPortMeta)` (`_backend.py:195`, with
`# type: ignore[misc]` on the metaclass at `:138`) makes mypy stop attribute-checking the annotated
type, and concluded the class had to be split before this story could proceed. **That measurement
was confounded by the import path**, not by the metaclass: its probe reached `TicketTransport`
through the unresolvable `rebar_reconciler` shim (→ `Any`) and compared it against a Protocol
declared locally in the same file (→ resolved). Re-run with the import path held constant, mypy
attribute-checks the metaclass-bearing Protocol normally — the `[attr-defined]` error above is
against today's `TicketTransport`, metaclass and all. Composition also survives: a
`class X(TicketTransport, SupportsComments, Protocol)` view is likewise attribute-checked.

`_TransportPortMeta` therefore stays exactly as it is, and this story does not touch it. It is
load-bearing for the RUNTIME side and independently verified as such: `isinstance` against a plain
`@runtime_checkable` Protocol goes through `ABCMeta`'s subclass cache and keeps answering `True`
after a member is deleted (measured), whereas `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` correctly flips to
`False`. Note also that `assert_transport_conforms()` ([rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]) is `hasattr`-based
and never calls `isinstance`, so it is immune to the cache by construction; the metaclass is what
keeps the *`isinstance` spelling* honest for the held-out conformance tests.

## The important subtlety — the EXISTING ratchet does not fix this

`pyproject.toml` documents a shrink-only mypy strictness ratchet (per-package
`disallow_untyped_defs`, enforced by `test_mypy_ratchet.py`), currently enabling
`rebar.graph.*` and `rebar.grounding.*`, with `_engine` in the exempt set awaiting promotion.

**Promoting `_engine` through that ratchet would NOT have prevented a357** — see the middle row
above: `client: Any` satisfies `disallow_untyped_defs` and remains completely blind. The requirement
is not 'annotate the params', it is 'annotate them AS THE PORT, resolvably'. A promotion done the
easy way (spraying `Any`) — or done with a port annotation imported through the `rebar_reconciler`
shim, which mypy widens to `Any` for you — would close the ratchet ticket while leaving this defect
fully intact. That is the outcome to guard against, and it now has two routes, not one.

## Scale (measured)

15 functions in `rebar_reconciler` take a `client`/`transport` parameter with NO annotation;
10 already annotate one. Sample untyped: `dispatch_one.create_one`, `dispatch_one.update_one`,
`dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter`, `batch_dispatch.delete_one`,
`apply_inbound.inbound_repair_property`. Any existing annotation that names a port type through the
`rebar_reconciler.` shim path counts as untyped for this story's purpose and must be re-pointed.

**Sizing probe, run:** annotating `client` on `dispatch_one.create_one` and `update_one` with a
relatively-imported `TicketTransport` produced exactly ONE new mypy error — `"TicketTransport" has
no attribute "add_comment"` at `dispatch_one.py:461`. That single finding is informative out of
proportion to its size; see the next section.

## The finding the sizing probe surfaced — capability members

`add_comment` is one of the four OPT-IN capability members (`set_relationship`,
`get_issuelinks_map`, `add_comment`, `get_comment_map`) that `_TransportPortMeta` carries as
metaclass attributes rather than class-body members, deliberately: `hasattr(TicketTransport,
"add_comment")` is `True` so the AST audit can attribute them, while `typing`'s protocol-attribute
collection never sees them, so a links-less or comment-less transport still conforms.

mypy does not consult metaclass attributes for a Protocol-typed value, so it reports these sites —
and it is RIGHT to. The existing AST audit
(`test_every_transport_member_the_core_reaches_for_is_declared`) cannot report them, because
`hasattr` says `True`. **mypy is strictly stronger than the audit here**, and this is the first
concrete demonstration of that.

The correct resolution at such a site is to NARROW the annotation to a composed view that names the
capability the site actually requires — verified to type-check:

    class _CommentingTransport(TicketTransport, SupportsComments, Protocol): ...

It is NOT to add `add_comment` to the `TicketTransport` class body (that would force every future
transport to provide a feature it was never obliged to have), and NOT to widen back to `Any`.

## Interaction with J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36], settled

J9 already landed `assert_transport_conforms()`, a RUNTIME conformance guard wired into both backend
factories, plus the AST audit. This story is their STATIC complement, not their replacement. All
three stay, and they catch different things:

* runtime guard — a transport ASSEMBLED without a required member, caught at construction, before
  any write.
* AST audit — a core module reaching for a member no port declares, caught for the always-required
  set.
* mypy — a core CALL SITE reaching for a member its annotated view does not offer, caught at
  authoring time, including the capability members the audit structurally cannot see.

Removing or weakening any of them is out of scope.

## Also explains [rebar:dbf9-3fc8-625d-4730]

The same `Any` is why Serena/Pyright returns a FALSE EMPTY for
`find_referencing_symbols('set_entity_property')` — no resolvable receiver type, so no references.
Note this cuts the same way as the mypy finding: the unresolvable `rebar_reconciler.` import is a
second, independent source of that blindness, so navigation only recovers where BOTH the annotation
and its import path are fixed.

## Approach

**Annotate as the PORT, import the PORT resolvably, then let mypy find the gaps.**

1. **Re-point the port import** in each core module that will carry an annotation: replace
   `from rebar_reconciler._backend import …` with `from ._backend import …` for the types used in
   annotations. Relative imports are already used in this package
   (`adapters/__init__.py`) and are correct at runtime under both module names, so this is not a
   runtime behaviour change. A `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded relative import is an acceptable variant
   where a module has a reason to keep its runtime import absolute.
2. **Annotate** each unannotated `client`/`transport` parameter with `TicketTransport`, or with a
   composed/capability Protocol where the site genuinely needs one.
3. **Probe before editing.** Run the annotation pass and record the resulting `[attr-defined]` list
   on this ticket BEFORE resolving it, so the change's size is known rather than discovered halfway.
   Expected shape, from the sizing probe: mostly capability members, a small tail of genuine port
   gaps.
4. **Treat every `[attr-defined]` as a FINDING, not noise.** Resolve each by either DECLARING the
   member on `TicketTransport` (the core genuinely always requires it) or NARROWING the annotation
   to a composed capability view (the member is opt-in). Never by widening back to `Any`, and never
   by reverting to the shim import path — those are the two ways this change can silently
   self-neutralise.

**Do NOT promote `_engine` through the strictness ratchet in this story.** The ratchet enables
`disallow_untyped_defs`, which `client: Any` satisfies while remaining completely blind. Promotion
and port-typing are separate changes and conflating them is how the easy version ships and closes
both.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` — re-point port imports to a mypy-resolvable path and
  annotate the `client`/`transport` parameters.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — declare any member mypy proves the core
  ALWAYS requires and the port omits; add composed capability views where sites need them. The
  `_TransportPortMeta` metaclass and `assert_transport_conforms()` are NOT modified.
- tests pinning that neither self-neutralising route passes (see Testing).
- a note in `pyproject.toml` / `docs/architecture.md` per the last AC.

**NOT in scope:** promoting `_engine` through the mypy strictness ratchet; changing
`_TransportPortMeta`, `assert_transport_conforms()`, or the AST audit; converting the package's
other 80-odd non-annotation imports to relative form (a separate, larger clean-up — this story
re-points only what its annotations need); any behaviour change whatsoever.

## Testing

* `make typecheck` is clean at the resulting strictness, and `make lint` passes.
* the full reconciler unit suite passes UNEDITED — this is a pure annotation + import-form change,
  so any test that needs editing means behaviour moved and the change has failed its own premise.
* the backend contract / conformance suites pass unchanged, demonstrating the runtime guard and the
  AST audit are untouched.
* **the blindness guard, which is the load-bearing test.** A check over the core reconciler that
  fails if a `client`/`transport` parameter is annotated `Any`, left bare, OR annotated with a port
  type imported through the unresolvable `rebar_reconciler.` path. All three are equivalent to no
  annotation at all under `mypy src/rebar`, and the third is the one a reviewer will not see.
* a NEGATIVE mypy probe, run and recorded: a scratch call to an undeclared member through a
  port-typed parameter in a core module must produce `[attr-defined]`, proving the annotation
  enforces something rather than merely being present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every `client`/`transport` parameter in the core reconciler is annotated with the PORT type
      (`TicketTransport`, or a capability/composed Protocol where the site needs one), NOT `Any`
- [ ] every such annotation names a type mypy actually RESOLVES — verified by `reveal_type`
      returning a `rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler...` type, never `Any`, for at least one parameter
      per touched module
- [ ] a scratch call to an undeclared member through one of those parameters produces
      `[attr-defined]` under `mypy src/rebar`; the transcript is recorded on this ticket
- [ ] every `[attr-defined]` the annotation pass produced is resolved by declaring the member on
      `TicketTransport` or by narrowing to a capability view — none by widening to `Any` and none by
      reverting an import to the `rebar_reconciler.` path; the full list and its per-item resolution
      is recorded on this ticket
- [ ] a test fails if a core `client`/`transport` param is annotated `Any`, left bare, or annotated
      through the unresolvable shim import path, so a future 'annotate it to pass the ratchet'
      change cannot silently reintroduce the blindness
- [ ] `_TransportPortMeta`, `assert_transport_conforms()`, and the AST audit are byte-unchanged, and
      the held-out conformance tests still pass — the static check is added ALONGSIDE the runtime
      guard, not in place of it
- [ ] `mypy src/rebar` is clean, and the reconciler unit + contract suites pass unedited
- [ ] the ratchet note in `pyproject.toml` / `docs/architecture.md` records BOTH defeat routes: that
      annotating as `Any` satisfies `disallow_untyped_defs` while defeating its purpose at port
      boundaries, AND that a port annotation imported via `rebar_reconciler.` is silently widened to
      `Any` by `ignore_missing_imports`
